Accounts & wallets

Track where your money actually sits

Add PHP or foreign-currency cash, bank accounts, e-wallets, savings, time deposits, Pag-IBIG MP2, or other money locations. Foreign balances stay in their native currency while SINOP shows a live reporting-currency equivalent. Transfers move money without counting as income or spending.

Total tracked money₱0.00
Usable money₱0.00
Reserved for goals₱0.00
Cold cash₱0.00
Banks & savings₱0.00
Time deposit & MP2₱0.00
E-wallets₱0.00
Account rules: Time Deposit and Pag-IBIG MP2 are treated as non-spendable asset accounts, so they never appear as sources for bills, purchases, or card payments. They can still receive transfers and be tracked as assets.

How balances work: each account starts from a balance snapshot: the amount you actually know and its exact Balance as of date. Transactions on or before that date are assumed to already be included in the snapshot, while later received income, actual spending, completed recurring commitments, transfers, card payments, and IOU cash movements change the running balance. Planned expenses do not reduce balances until they become actual.

Goal savings: assigning saved goal money to an account only earmarks part of that existing balance. It does not create a second deduction or transfer. The account will show total balance, usable/unreserved money, and the amount reserved for goals.

Accounting rule: lending or borrowing changes the linked account balance, but it is not treated as ordinary monthly income or spending. Repayments also move cash and reduce the IOU balance without being counted a second time in the budget.

Interest / fee: this tracker uses a simple one-time percentage added to the original principal. It is an IOU balance tracker, not an APR/amortization engine.

How XP works

Healthy actions earn progress

XP is recalculated from your current data. If you undo a qualifying action—such as marking a bill unpaid—the related XP is removed automatically.

Live rewards: XP and live badges—including First Save, Investor Started, Bills Cleared, Budget Guardian, streaks, and Statement Cleared—recalculate from your current data. If the qualifying data is removed or returned to zero, the badge locks again. Lifetime milestone badges remain unlocked once legitimately achieved.
Save moneyNew money added to Savings / Time Deposit accounts, or an untracked savings amount.+15+
InvestNew money added to MP2 / investment accounts, or a dated untracked investment. Up to 2 XP-earning contributions per month, at least 10 days apart.+20+
Hit 10%+Put at least 10% of monthly income toward savings or investments.+20
Pay billsMark all active recurring bills paid for a tracked month.+20
Stay on budgetKeep configured spending categories within their limits.+15
Finish goalsFully fund a purchase or savings goal.+40

Your money story

User manual

Learn the planner with confidence

This guide explains how the planner treats planned money, actual money, accounts, daily envelopes, bills, cards, IOUs, goals, and reports. Follow the quick-start path once, then use the feature reference whenever you need it.

1. Choose monthEverything is reviewed by budget month.
2. Confirm incomeOnly received pay credits accounts.
3. Track accountsKnow exactly where your money sits.
4. Plan daily useAllowance rolls over and may go negative.
5. Log actual spendQuick spend or detailed spending entries.
6. ReviewOverview, dashboard, statements, rewards.

Quick start

Recommended setup order

Set the planner up in this order so balances and daily-budget calculations have a reliable starting point.

1
Choose the budget month

The month picker at the top controls which income receipts, bills, spending, daily allowance, statements, and analytics you are reviewing.

2
Add your accounts first

Create cash, bank, e-wallet, savings, Time Deposit, MP2, or investment accounts. Enter the balance you actually see and the exact date that balance was true—you do not need to reconstruct the first day of the month.

3
Add income sources

Link income to the account that actually receives it. For recurring pay, confirm each payment occurrence only when it arrives.

4
Enter commitments

Add recurring expenses, savings, investments, debt repayments, and transfers. Complete them only when the real movement happens.

5
Build the daily plan

Edit today's Allowance, Transportation, and Miscellaneous directly, and log actual spending independently from the plan. A ₱0 plan never prevents an actual transaction; SINOP records the difference as overspending. Use Day details only for account, notes, or another date.

6
Use Overview every day

Confirm what was received, check cash after IOUs, see daily rollover, and use Quick spend for small purchases throughout the day.

Best practice: set a Default spending account under Customize. New spending-side dropdowns will use it automatically, while you can still override the account for any individual transaction.

Key concepts

Planned money is not the same as actual money

The planner deliberately separates expectations from transactions. This is the most important concept to understand.

Planned income vs. income receivedPlanning tells you what should arrive. Receipt confirmations tell the accounts what actually arrived.

Income

Record what you expect, confirm what you receive

An income row describes the source and frequency. Receipt controls determine when the linked account is actually credited.

Recurring payUse frequency-specific confirmations for pay that arrives more than once in a month.
Income rowTwice monthly
Salary
₱44,000
Maribank
1st payment2nd payment
  • For Salary, checking a payment opens Attendance adjustments first; the payment is confirmed only after you save.
  • Only confirmed occurrences count as received.
  • Each confirmed occurrence also has a received date; edit it if the default is not the actual credit date.
  • Weekly and biweekly sources show multiple occurrence controls when applicable.
  • One-time, monthly, quarterly, and annual entries use a single confirmation when due.
Salary deductionsEmployment treatment can estimate payroll deductions before calculating expected take-home pay.
  1. Choose the employment treatment in the income row.
  2. Open the salary breakdown to review deduction assumptions.
  3. Use attendance adjustments when absences, lateness, or undertime affect payroll.
  4. Confirm the actual pay occurrence only when deposited.
Account rule: linking an income source to an account does not mean all planned pay is already in that account. The balance increases only for received occurrences dated after that account's balance snapshot. A received occurrence on or before the snapshot remains in monthly income reports but is not added again.
Multi-currency accounts: choose a currency per account. SINOP keeps the ledger balance in that native currency and uses a cached Frankfurter reference rate only for the current reporting-currency equivalent and combined totals. Cross-currency transfers lock the conversion used for that movement, so later FX changes revalue the remaining balance without rewriting the historical transfer.
Untouched-month rule: The planner does not assume that recurring salary or other income was received in historical months you never tracked. Past months remain at zero until you explicitly confirm a receipt or record month-specific activity. This keeps Annual Wrapped, statements, and trend charts from inventing January–July income just because a recurring source exists.

Accounts & wallets

Track where the money actually sits

Accounts are the ledger layer of the planner. They reconcile actual income, spending, bill payments, transfers, card payments, and IOU cash movements.

Account typeUse it forImportant behavior
Cold cashCash kept physically.Spendable and eligible as a default spending source.
Bank / SavingsPayroll, checking, savings, ordinary deposits.Starts from a dated balance snapshot, then applies only later linked activity.
E-walletDigital spending balances.Spendable like a bank account.
Time Deposit / MP2Longer-term savings or investment placement.Tracked as assets but intentionally excluded from ordinary spending-source dropdowns.
InvestmentOther investment balances.Can receive tracked contributions; use projections where available.
Starting mid-month: if you begin on August 10 and your bank shows ₱25,000, enter ₱25,000 with Balance as of August 10. An August 2 salary can still appear in August Income, but it is tagged as included in the starting balance and is not credited to the bank again. Income received after August 10 does change the account. Use Reconcile later if the planner and the real account differ.
Transfer moneyChoose From, To, amount, and date.

A same-currency transfer subtracts and adds the same amount. A cross-currency transfer stores the source amount, converted destination amount, and the FX rate used so the movement remains an internal transfer rather than income or spending.

Default spending accountSet it once under Customize.

New spending-side dropdowns automatically start with this account instead of Untracked. Existing saved transactions are not retroactively reassigned.

The detailed allowance, transportation, miscellaneous, account, notes, and Use full controls live inside each day's Details modal. Weekday/weekend styling is informational; your actual days off are customizable.

Spending & recurring

Separate planned purchases from actual cash movement

Use Spending for irregular purchases and Recurring for obligations that repeat. Only actual payment activity should reduce tracked accounts.

Variable spendingShopping, dining, household, entertainment, and other non-recurring items.
  1. Add the date, description, category, and amount.
  2. Use Planned while it is only an intention.
  3. Switch to Actual when you really spend it.
  4. Select the payment account or card so the ledger can move correctly.
Recurring commitmentsClassify repeating cash movements before you complete them.
  1. Expense — rent, utilities, subscriptions and other consumption.
  2. Savings — moves money into Savings or Time Deposit without counting as an expense.
  3. Investment — moves money into MP2 or an Investment account and counts toward wealth-building.
  4. Debt repayment — creates a real repayment against a linked IOU.
  5. Transfer — moves money between your own accounts without changing total cash.
MP2 example: create “MP2 contribution” as Investment, choose your MP2 account as the destination, and set the monthly amount. When you complete it, the funding account decreases and MP2 increases automatically.
Do not double-enter: when you complete a Savings, Investment, or Transfer commitment, the planner creates the account movement automatically. Do not also add the same transfer under Accounts.
KKB / group expensesSplit shared trips, meals, or gala expenses fairly.
  1. Create a KKB trip and add the members.
  2. Enter each shared item as a row.
  3. Tick the members who shared that item.
  4. Choose who paid upfront.
  5. Use the settlement plan to see who should reimburse whom, then record payments as they happen.
BarkadaKeep reusable groups of people without exposing your personal finances.
  1. Create a Barkada and add members using their Google email.
  2. SINOP creates a separate shared Drive file for the group roster.
  3. The invited person signs in with that Google account and joins through the invite link.
  4. Use the Barkada roster to start a KKB without retyping everyone.
Privacy boundary: Barkada members can access the shared group file, not your accounts, salary, spending, goals, or private SINOP cloud file.
Overview vs. DashboardUse Overview for today's operational picture; use Dashboard for patterns and decisions.
  • Overview: received income, current balances, daily budget, quick spend, IOUs, cards, and immediate status.
  • Dashboard: trends, category analysis, fixed-term outlooks, and planning guidance.
Daily budget rule: unpaid recurring bills are not reserved inside the Daily budget card because that feature treats your recurring-bill money as separately funded. Planned Spending items and future daily envelopes still affect the day-to-day planning calculation.

Credit cards & IOUs

Track obligations without pretending they are ordinary cash

Credit cards delay the cash outflow until statement payment. Loans and IOUs track who owes whom separately from ordinary income and spending.

Credit cardsCharges increase the card obligation; cash decreases only when the statement is paid.
  • Link spending or recurring bills to the card.
  • Review charges and statement totals.
  • Record the statement payment from the actual bank/cash account.
  • Installments remain visible until their remaining terms are completed.
Loans & IOUsUse Borrowed when you owe someone; use Lent when someone owes you.
  • Borrowed money may increase the linked account when cash is received.
  • Repayments reduce the linked account and the remaining obligation.
  • Outstanding borrowed IOUs reduce the Overview's Cash after IOUs.
  • Money owed to you is shown separately and does not count as cash until received.

Goals & rewards

Turn leftover capacity into intentional progress

Goals plan future purchases or savings targets. Rewards recognize consistent actions without changing your real financial balances.

GoalsSet a target, deadline, priority, and optional account allocation.
  1. Create the goal and target amount.
  2. Choose a saving strategy or use the planner recommendation.
  3. Record contributions as money is actually set aside.
  4. Assign saved goal money to an account only to earmark it; this does not create another cash deduction.
RewardsXP, levels, badges, and streaks reflect your tracking habits. Use View all levels—or the level chip beside Help—to browse all 15 levels, five stages, XP ranges, and level badges.

Rewards are motivational metadata. They do not add cash, change account balances, or alter the budget. If a qualifying action is removed or reversed, reward calculations may update accordingly.

Reports & backup

Review history and protect your data

SINOP saves locally first. You can optionally synchronize one private JSON copy through Google Drive app data, while statements and exports remain available for review and independent backup.

StatementsGenerate a monthly or annual ledger view from recorded activity.
  • Review debit and credit entries. Debits show money coming in; credits show money going out.
  • Use monthly mode for a selected budget month.
  • Use annual mode for a year-level review.
  • Account and transaction data determine the ledger rows.
Backup and restoreUse a full JSON backup before major changes or moving browsers/computers.
  • Export full backup (.json) to preserve your data.
  • Import a backup to restore that saved state.
  • Export the selected month to CSV for tabular analysis.
  • Without Google Drive sync, data stays local to this browser. With Drive sync enabled, SINOP keeps a private app-data copy while local saving remains active.
WrappedYour visual monthly or yearly money story.

Wrapped opens as a full-screen animated money story. Scroll or use Next/Previous to move through scenes with changing backgrounds, animated figures, spending highlights, no-spend days, Daily allowance behavior, recurring commitments, wealth streaks, goals, accounts, rewards, IOUs, and KKB activity. Use Replay to watch the story again.

CustomizeControl design and defaults without rewriting your financial history.
  • Theme, colors, compact layout, and dashboard visibility.
  • Financial rules, category budgets, payment methods, and reminder settings.
  • Default spending account for new payment-source dropdowns.
  • Design reset does not erase financial records.

Planning system

From daily decisions to month close

The newer planning tools share the same recorded data rather than creating a second budget beside your real one.

Activity, Inbox & JournalCapture quickly, then keep a searchable history.
  • Timeline combines actual financial events across modules.
  • Money Inbox holds uncategorized purchases without changing balances until processed.
  • Journal notes explain unusual months and life events.
Calendar & TodayKnow what matters before spending.
  • Today highlights safe daily budget, upcoming obligations, income confirmations, and runway.
  • Calendar places due dates, received income, spending, goals, and notes on one month view.
Forecast & RunwayProject instead of guessing.
  • Forecast uses future recurring plans plus an actual-spending baseline.
  • Runway shows normal, essential, and bare-minimum coverage if income stopped.
  • Money Autopsy explains the selected month's actual result.
Decision LabSimulate without posting transactions.
  • Can I afford this? tests liquidity and monthly burden.
  • Decision Compare evaluates cash vs installments.
  • Scenario Mode models alternate futures.
  • Goal Trade-offs shows which targets move when one is prioritized.
Month Open & CloseSeparate planning from finalized history.

Opening a month is an explicit planning action; it does not mark income received. Closing a month records that you reviewed income, spending, commitments, accounts, and notes. Untouched historical months remain excluded from annual actuals.

Command Palette & SearchUse Ctrl/⌘ K anywhere.

Search accounts, goals, bills, cards, IOUs, KKB, notes, and timeline events—or type quick commands such as spend 250 coffee, inbox 1200 groceries, or note moved apartment.

Troubleshooting

Common questions

Use these checks before assuming a balance is wrong.

Why did my account not increase even though I added income?

Check whether the income occurrence is marked received, has the correct received date, and links to the correct account. If the received date is on or before that account's Balance as of date, the planner assumes the money is already included in the starting snapshot and deliberately does not add it again.

Why did my daily budget go negative?

You spent more than the cumulative planned daily envelope available through today. The negative amount is intentional and carries forward until future daily plans recover the deficit.

I clicked Use all by mistake. How do I reverse it?

The button changes to Undo all. It removes only the automatic entries created by that action; manual Quick spend transactions remain untouched.

Why does a transfer not change total tracked money?

A transfer is internal movement. The source account decreases by the same amount the destination increases, so your total assets do not change.

Why is a Time Deposit or MP2 not available for ordinary spending?

Those account types are intentionally treated as non-spendable/locked assets. They can receive transfers or contributions but are not offered as routine bill or purchase payment sources.

What does Untracked mean in a payment dropdown?

The expense still affects budget spending, but no specific tracked account is reduced. Set a Default spending account under Customize if most day-to-day purchases use one account.

What should I back up?

Use Customize → Data portability → Export full backup (.json). Keep the JSON file if you plan to change browser profiles, clear site data, or move to another computer.

Tip: use the User manual when you need detail and the guided tour when you want a fast refresher.

Interactive setup

Don't tour SINOP. Build it.

This walkthrough asks for the few things SINOP needs to become useful immediately. You will enter real starting information and finish with a working month instead of an empty app and a slideshow.

What we'll build together

Nine short steps. Fresh installs stay in setup until the essentials are configured.

1Your starting monthNo fake history before the month you choose.
2Your real balancesCurrent snapshots prevent double-counting.
3Your routineIncome, commitments, and daily spending.
4Your goalsOptional, but ready when you are.
5What's already happenedIncome only counts when you confirm it.
6A usable systemForecast, calendar, Wrapped, and decisions start with real inputs.
Important: recurring salary is a plan, not an actual receipt. Historical months are never backfilled unless you explicitly record them.
Already use SINOP on another device?Sign in to Google Drive and restore the private SINOP cloud copy instead of rebuilding setup.
Start month

Where should your money story begin?

Pick the month you're actually starting to track. Anything before it remains untouched unless you deliberately go back and record it.

Month rule: choosing a month lets you plan it. Actual income stays zero until you confirm payments that really arrived.
Accounts

Where is your money right now?

Enter current balances as snapshots, not reconstructed history. If today's balance already includes earlier salary, SINOP won't add that salary again before the snapshot date.

Use a balance you can verify. Never enter account numbers, passwords, or credentials.
Income

How does money usually come in?

Add income as schedules. For weekly, biweekly, or twice-monthly sources, enter the amount per payment. You'll confirm what actually arrived near the end.

Recurring commitments

What keeps coming back?

Rent, utilities, subscriptions, recurring savings, investments, and transfers belong here. Debt repayments can be linked later after you create the IOU.

Daily plan

What does an ordinary day cost?

This creates Daily allowance envelopes for working days. Unused amounts roll forward; overspending can push the envelope negative.

Regular days off
Goals

What are you trying to make possible?

Goals are optional. Add what you're intentionally saving toward and SINOP can model timing, trade-offs, and funding progress.

Already happened

What income has actually arrived?

This is the line between planning and reality. Check only payments that truly reached you. Leave future or missed payments unchecked.

Snapshot-safe: a confirmed payment on or before an account's balance date is treated as already included in that snapshot.
Ready

Your starting system is ready.

Review what you configured. Starting SINOP opens the selected month for planning and takes you directly to your Today briefing.

Ready to start

You can change any of this later. Nothing in earlier untouched months is created automatically.

We'll only ask for information that changes how the planner works.
